body: It was heavily laden with mist sometimes reducing the visibility to a few meters. The sprawling water body was swallowed by the mist reaching up to its surface. With the gentle breeze there were times that the mist got thinned out exposing all that beauty which was kept under its cover. The park area was undergoing rejuvenation with flower beds been redone. There was no colour but the topiaries in the form of birds were the attraction at this time. A ground level scorpion shaped design constituting of planting beds with Alternanthera ground cover planted on it was still in the developing stage but was eye-catching. Datura the trumpet flower in two shades were the significant blooms. Wet condition was the spoiler with flowering bedding plants been badly affected making a few surviving flowers also to droop. Only flowers that could standout were the Arum Lilies.

body: I’ve been visiting Gregory Lake since my childhood — for over 22 years — and it’s a place that holds many cherished memories. The landscaping is lovely, the cool climate is refreshing, and it’s still a wonderful spot to visit with family. The lake area itself is scenic and peaceful, especially for walks, picnics, or simply enjoying the view.However, I was disappointed during my recent visit to see that the bicycle track area on the opposite side of the lake is not well maintained. There was a lot of garbage pulled out from the lake, and the smell was quite unpleasant. Even worse, the path was littered with poop from ponies and horses, making it difficult — and unsafe — for children to play or ride in that area.It’s sad to see such a beautiful and historic place neglected in parts. With a bit more attention to cleanliness and maintenance, Gregory Lake could easily be one of the top attractions in Nuwara Eliya again. I truly hope the authorities take action soon.
title: A Beautiful Lake with Great Memories — But Needs Better Maintenance

body: The Lake takes its name from British Governor, Sir William Gregory, who had the reservoir constructed in 1873 to aid electricity generation. Apparently it was never used for this purpose, becoming a place for recreation and leisure instead. In recent years the area has been upgraded and a variety of leisure facilities added. You can enjoy a picnic, paddle a swan shaped boat on the lake among the other speedboats, jetskis and windsurfers, take a stroll around the perimeter or go for a pony ride. Nothing seems to be free here, every activity has a price, really a pittance when compared to similar activities in Australia. Worth a visit even if only to enjoy the views.

As we were getting ready to leave the city on the way to Nanu Oya Railway Station (for the train ride to Ella) we stopped for an hour or so at Gregory Lake Park. It was on a Sunday, the weather was nice and sunny, and a lot of locals were enjoying the day off in the park. Whole families with kids and grandparents enjoying a picnic on the grass, youngsters racing motor boats on the lake, others just taking it easier with paddle boats, young lovers walking hand-in-hand around the lake, people just sitting on a bench or on the grass talking or sharing a meal, etc. There were no foreign tourists and it was a good place to observe the locals having fun...

The area also suffers from an excess of accumulated rubbish both in and out of the water. As you pass along the shoreline adjacent to the main road the area has been established as a park which costs 200 rupees for foreigners to enter and where you can partake in water sports, get food and drink etc. There was a jet ski whizzing around, a couple of motor boss offering trips and pedal boats for hire, all back by a general hullabaloo no music and drums. The other side of the lake was quieter if you’re just looking for a walk although it does have a locked vehicle barrier which we just passed under (nobody came to challenge us). body: Nuwara Elliya in the central Hills of Sri Lanka which is dubbed the little England is also reminiscent of Switzerland. Lake Gregory located a couple of kilometers away from the city centre makes it look like Lucerne in Switzerland. Of course, it doesn't snow here in Sri Lanka though temperature can drop to about 6 degrees Celsius. It's a lake that has no particular shape, but is much longer than it's wide. There's a very long walking track around the lake that's great for strolling. There is facility to take boat rides of different sorts including paddle boats, regular boats, speed boats and jet skies. There's a floating restaurant by the side of the lake. A sizeable car park is located next to the lake. Helicopter rides are available from a helipad adjoining the lake. I would suggest you to approach the lake from Upper Lake Road side as well. This allows you to have a glimpse of the city over the lake. There are many restaurants on the side of the Badulla /Bandarawela Road that forms one border of the lake. The surroundings of the lake has a lot to offer kids to enjoy. This high elevation located lake is simply breathtaking. Any tourist visiting the city should not miss the Gregory Lake.
title: A place reminiscent of Switzerland's lakes

body: My partner and I visited the lake today for a walk around. At the entrance nearest town (by the small kids amusement rides) we were charged 200 LKR each and told we could walk the full 4km around the lake with this ticket by the guard. Local adults are charged 50 LKR but I understand that in Sri Lanka it is common to charge higher prices to tourists. We walked anitclockwise and the first section of the walk was lovely past food stalls and gardens. It would be much nicer if all the plastic garbage was cleared from the water!!The path around the lake is not fully built so we exited at the bridge, crossed and walked along the road for a while. We then tried to enter near the bike hire area and were told our tickets were not valid and we had to pay 200 LKR each again!! We were outraged at the stupidity of it! There is no way to walk all the way around without exiting and re-entering. Our tickets were the same as the ones they were trying to sell us again and our tickets had the date on them. We were so angry that greed would prompt these municipal ticket offices to not be honest to us in the first place, and then have an obviously stupid system in place. We refused to pay and walked along the road.It's worth mentioning that the next security gate we came across (about 150m along) was without staff so anyone could easily enter for free at this point anyway!Overall it was a nice walk but I would not want to recommend it based on the ridiculous ticket system and the need to walk along roads for substantial sections.
title: Overcharge for tourists!!

body: Location Nuwara EliyaCoordinates 6.957°N 80.780°ECoordinates: 6.957°N 80.780°EType ReservoirBasin countries Sri LankaBuilt 1873Surface area 91.2 ha (225 acres)Surface elevation 1,874 m (6,148 ft)Islands OneSettlements Nuwara EliyaLake Gregory (Sinhalese: ග්‍රෙගරි වැව), sometimes also called Gregory Lake or Gregory Reservoir, is a reservoir in heart of the tea country hill city, Nuwara Eliya, Sri Lanka. Lake Gregory was constructed during the period of British Governor Sir William Gregory in 1873. The lake and the surrounding area make up the Gregory Lake Area.HistoryThe area was originally a swampy bog at the foot of the small hills that border the town. In 1873 Sir William Gregory authorised the damming of the Thalagala stream, which originates from Mount Pidurutalagala, in order to make more land available for the expansion of the town. In 1881 the lake was stocked with trout by Mr C. J. R. Le Mesurier (Assistant Government Agent for Nuwara Eliya).In 1913 the waters of the lake were directed into a tunnel which flows to a hydro power station at 'Blackpool' between the town and Nanu Oya.The power station continues to supply electricity to the town to this day. In British times Lake Gregory was used for water sports and recreational activities.

There were several types of boats to rent including paddle boats and noisy jetskis and even though it was a cold day there were a few locals on the jetskis. Towards the south of the lake i had to walk by the road until i was on the east side where i passed through a gate and continued my walk by the lake. It seems that the eastern side of the lake is being developed as the paths were new and the only thing available ere kayaks for rent.Lake Gregory was an artificial lake, constructed by 1873 by the British Governor, Sir William Gregory. I noticed a few people fishing in the lake, without much success.
title: A lovely walk round Lake Gregory

body: Very clean and relaxing lakeside walk. Good views. Choice of boat, jet ski rides, pony rides. Small entrance fee for vehicle and each persons. Passed a couple of hours.

title: Amazing view

body: The first day we visited Gregory Lake we arrived just in time for the fog to roll in.They wanted us to pay to walk around the lake so we declined as we couldn’t see 5m in front of us.We went back the next day on Independence Day and all the locals were there having drinks and playing cricket.It was entertaining.The unfortunate thing with Gregory lake is that they don’t have any idea about picking up rubbish.It was soooo polluted with plastic and rubbish everywhere.It was a bit confronting coming from Australia where this kind of rubbish would cause National outcry.Dead animals in the canals joining the lake.Not a pleasant sight.Worth Having a brief look but they need to take the rubbish in hand if they want it to be a class attraction
title: So polutted and charged to walk around

body: We were very impressed and taken up by Gregory lake. The lake is very large with lush green surroundings. One can sit and enjoy the nature which is the greenery around the lake and the urban dwellings beyond. There are number of water sports activities and eateries around. If one is on a longer stay in Nuwara Eliya it is of moderate walking distance from most of the hotels or a short drive by a vehicle. It is a place wort visiting either for sight seeing or for a relaxing stroll.

body: A reasonably big lake with nice green lawns surrounded by misty mountains.We spent a good 2 hours there at the lake and then had lunch at an indian restaurant overlooking the lake. The speed boat ride is charged about LKR 4500 for a 10 minute speed boat ride. Initially we were a little reluctant if we should take it or not, but then we went ahead and had an amazing time. The kids enjoyed it a lot enough for them to recollect that as one of the highlights of the trip after we were back home.One common aspect that you have to get used to is foreign nationals are charged an entry fee for almost every place you visit (which are either free of cost for locals or significantly lower) and gregory lake is no exception to that.
